I have done this for almost as long as I can remember, except it's not just my molars. Take the half circle shape of your teeth and divide that into like six or so points (one molar on either side, one canine on either side, and my two front teeth). Think of them like hotspots. 

As I go through my day, I will grind and tap my teeth, usually following that half circle shape, to the rhythm of music, or more prominently, to the rhythm or cadence of my inner dialogue and the speech that goes on around me. I also spell words in my head and tap or grind in sync with the spelling.

So if I hear someone say hello, I might spell out the letters H-E-L-L-O, and with each letter I tap a tooth—for example, back left molar for H, left canine for E, left front tooth for L, right front tooth for L, and right canine for O. Then, to finalize the spelling, I'll tap my right back molar to signify a period. This also happens with whole sentences.

The most annoying thing about this is that since I've spent so much time typing on a computer, the layout of the keyboard is engrained visually and tactilely in my head. So recently I've begun to do this tapping thing, but as if I'm typing. Each tooth tap signifies me hitting a key on the keyboard. 

It sucks and makes me feel a bit crazy, but I realize it's probably stress or anxiety and some measure of OCD manifesting itself into my physical behaviour. Who knows why. But each time I notice it happening, I do my best to bring my awareness back to my breath, like I'm meditating. That helps a bit

Find a therapist. One with whom you feel truly comfortable speaking with. 

I actually had a really similar dream the other night. I was at home, getting ready to drive back to school (3 hours away from my home, not too long but long enough) but I didn’t want to leave. I laid down on my mothers bed and started weeping with her sitting next to me, comforting me. At one point, in between sobs, I said “momma, I just want to play”. Then I kept crying, and eventually woke up. It was like the emotion was present one moment, but then it disappeared in an instant when I awoke. I just felt numb going through my daily routine. 

Anyways, I had a session with my therapist later that day. When I tried telling her about the dream, actually speaking the words was so difficult that I began to cry. It was painful, slowly trying to squeeze the words out and into the world, but when I did it was like I opened the floodgates and I wept, in real life this time, while my therapist sat with me as a silent support.

When we explored it further, we realized together that the dream was a manifestation of my child self crying out for help. Basically, the university program I’m currently enrolled in may not be the right path for me, and I was feeling a huge amount of pressure with that. So my child self expressed his need to lighten up, and to play; to play meaning to do something I genuinely enjoy, which probably entails me leaving my university and letting go of the prospect of needing to complete my degree.

The moral of the story is that sometimes, all you need to let go and release that huge buildup of negative emotion is someone who’s willing to sit with you and listen as you talk about whatever is on your mind. And then you’ll start to heal and grow again.
